newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Peronists expect quorum for Argentine tax debate.
newsitem.headline: Peronists expect quorum for Argentine tax debate.

text.p: Argentina's ruling Peronist Party is confident it will get a quorum in the Chamber of Deputies Wednesday to debate Economy Minister Roque Fernandez's austerity package, Peronist Congressmen said.

The lower house was due to convene at 3 p.m. (2 p.m. EDT/ 1800 GMT) and will allow for one hour to muster a quorum. Peronist deputy Erman Gonzalez, a former economy and defense minister, Menem, said 129 of the 131-strong Peronist majority pledged to be present. They need 130 deputies for a quorum.
"We also have a commitment from some provincial party deputies; just one of them would let us to begin the session," Gonzalez told reporters.

President Carlos Menem's government suffered a humiliating setback in Congress last Wednesday when it failed to get a quorum in the lower house to debate austerity measures, including major taxes hikes, which it hopes will cut back a looming $6.6 billion budget deficit.
When only 119 Peronist deputies arrived, the opposition Radical Party and Frepaso coalition decided not to attend the session.

Menem has lashed out at Peronist deputies who failed to show up and his aides have recruited the support of far-right and provincial deputies for a bill he hopes will boost revenue by $600 million with fuel and income tax hikes.

Radical Party whip Federico Storani said this time his bloc would wait to see if the Peronists raise a quorum, but if they do "we will participate in the debate because we are not going to run away from giving our position."

He made it clear the Radicals were "absolutely opposed" to the bill, as is the Frepaso. The latter coalition's leader, Carlos "Chacho" Alvarez, said this weekend his deputies would show up, adding that quorom-blocking maneuvers should not be a permanent tactic.
